text: The year was 1890, and the last natural forest in the industrial heart of Europe was a spectacle that many traveled miles to behold. Arthur, a young botanist, stood in awe among the ancient trees, a leather-bound journal in hand as he recorded notes about species that had become legends. This sacred grove, unbeknownst to him, was about to become the centerpiece of a historic preservation effort that would challenge the soot-choked metropolis of Paris, France, encroaching upon the natural world.
